title: What is Life All About?
description: In this program Dr. Rashad Khalifa argues that the world's biggest problem is neither war, disease nor poverty but that people do not know who they are, mistaking the body they see in a mirror for the self. He distinguishes body from soul, calls the body a garment worn for fifty or a hundred years, and observes that people feed the body three meals a day while giving the real person nothing, describing the soul as literally a piece of the breath God breathed into Adam and claiming it can grow to immense size when nourished. He says the nourishment is a specific method rather than vague spirituality or ordinary supplication: five daily contacts with God following what he compares to the numerical combination of a safe, with fasting as a further practice, and he offers newly obtained mathematically coded evidence as his authority. Citing the Barbara Hutton story and Eddie Murphy's interview with Barbara Walters as cases of wealth without happiness, he closes by inviting viewers to examine the physical evidence free of charge, giving an address on East 6th Street in Tucson and a telephone number.

title: Who is GOD?
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa argues that idol worship persists because people do not grasp the greatness of God, and devotes the sermon to establishing that scale from what he presents as established scientific facts. He works outward from the solar system, whose sunlight reaches Earth in four minutes and whose span runs to billions of miles, to the Milky Way, which light would take a hundred thousand years to cross, to a neighboring galaxy two million light years away, to a universe of a billion galaxies and a billion trillion stars measuring some 26 billion light years across, pausing to calculate that merely counting a quintillion stars at one per second would take 32 billion years. He then states, on the authority of the Quran and its mathematical code, that this universe is the smallest and innermost of seven, so that no number can express the circumference of the outermost, and cites Sura 39:67 on the heavens held in God's hand as an allegory for that greatness. He concludes that against this scale it is blasphemous to attribute to God a son, wife or mother, or to idolize Muhammad, Jesus, Mary or a saint, asking what role any of them played in setting the synchronized rotation of the moon or the precision of the orbits. Recording date: this is the Friday sermon of 4 August 1988. It was also uploaded separately as a dated Friday sermon, and that upload was the only place the date was stated; the two were proven to be one recording by a flat timestamp offset across sixteen minutes, so the duplicate entry was merged into this one and its dating carried over. This transcript is the fuller of the two, being the only one to include the opening takbirs from 00:01:19.

On this account the misery in the world is the visible result of Satan's incompetence, while those who side with God's view belong to a kingdom he describes as free of illness, financial trouble and even headaches. Participants Dean Mahmoud and Loretta raise questions about systemic bribery in Egypt and the Philippines, prompting Dr. Khalifa to argue that bribery is strictly prohibited unless forced by life-threatening circumstances. Latifa queries the command to be straightforward in 2:189, leading to a discussion on diplomatic communication. Dr. Khalifa shares lighthearted anecdotes about Masouda throwing a pillow at Abdullah and Catherine putting shaving cream in Abdullah's shoe instead of Erol's. He analyzes the rules of war in 2:190-195, contrasting Quranic self-defense with the Iraq-Iran war, and promotes his Arabic language course. After a recitation of Al-Fatihah, the group discusses how Salat wipes out inadvertent sins under 11:114 and 29:45. Dr. Khalifa argues against extra fasting outside Ramadan, dismissing Sunni traditions of fasting on Mondays and Thursdays as non-Quranic innovations. He explains the conversion of sins to credits in 25:70 upon repenting from idol worship, emphasizing continuous repentance. Finally, he outlines the rules of Hajj in 2:196-198, recounting a trip with his father, and addresses objections regarding the Ka'aba and Safa and Marwah as potential idol worship.

title: Messenger Audio 71 — Friday Sermon — Erasing Sins and Reliance on Quran Alone (Rashad)
description: Rashad Khalifa delivers a Friday sermon at the Masjid Tucson focusing on the absolute requirement of sinlessness for entering Paradise. Drawing from Dean Majul's previous lectures on Adam and Eve's expulsion from Eden for a single sin, Khalifa argues that believers must erase all sins before death. He outlines two methods for erasing sins: immediate repentance (tawbah) and paying for them through worldly trials, assigning a hypothetical ten-thousand-dollar price to adultery. He examines Suras 4:17-18 and 39:53, noting that Moses was forgiven for murder due to immediate repentance. Citing Suras 4:48 and 4:116, he identifies idol worship as the sole unforgivable offense, criticizing Christians for idolizing Jesus and Muslims for idolizing Muhammad. In his second sermon, Khalifa asserts that Arabic fluency is not required to understand the Quran, citing Sura 41:44 to argue that God reveals the message directly to sincere hearts. He condemns traditional reliance on Hadith, Sunnah, ijma, and qiyas, citing Suras 17:45-46, 6:112-113, 39:45, and 40:10-12 to support the doctrine of Quran alone. During the subsequent question-and-answer session, he rejects belief in the evil eye as idol worship, explains that death occurs only by divine decree, and addresses double rewards for converts. The recording ends with a study of Sura 2:196 and the rituals of Hajj and Umrah.

title: Messenger Audio 72 — Friday Sermon — Satanic Intrusion in Rituals and Adam's Disobedience (Rashad)
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa leads a Qur'an study session on Sura 2 (Al-Baqarah), discussing verses 158 and 196 through 213, alongside study group attendees Dean Majul, Jahan, and Abib. Dr. Khalifa argues that visiting the Prophet's tomb constitutes idol worship, while clarifying rules for Hajj pilgrimage, including expiation fasting, commercial benefits during Hajj, and the symbolic stoning of Satan at Mina. He and Dean Majul address Abraham's sacrifice test, noting the Qur'an never states God commanded the killing of his son, and explain the seven universes. Attendees recite verses 204 through 213, prompting discussions on hypocrites with impressive rhetoric, sinful pride, and Satan tempting believers to add unauthorized steps to religious practices like ablution. Dr. Khalifa reflects on facing persecution for upholding the Qur'an alone. Following the discussion, Dean Majul delivers a Friday Khutba focusing on Adam's disobedience in Sura 20:115, asserting it stemmed from Satan-induced forgetfulness rather than malicious intent. Citing Suras 15:29, 32:9, 51:56, and 91:7-10, Majul explores the divine spirit breathed into humanity, defining soul growth as actualizing innate capacities to know God and practice compassion. He shares an Arabic proverb regarding six urgent matters, including immediate repentance, before concluding with Sura 2:152 and leading the Friday prayer.
