Quran Study 01 — Surah 72:19-28 & 73 — Jinns (Catherine)
description: Catherine leads a study of Sura 72 (verses 19-28) and Sura 73 (verses 1-20), reading from Dr. Rashad Khalifa's upcoming translation of the Quran. She discusses the reaction of disbelievers when God alone is advocated, noting how their hearts shrink in aversion due to their egos. Dr. Khalifa explains the purpose of human existence as a chance to redeem ourselves after siding with Satan in the heavenly society. He argues that the true size of a believer's soul in the Hereafter is massive, while disbelievers shrink to the size of cats or ants. Edip Yuksel raises a question about the number of guards in Hell, leading to a debate with Dr. Khalifa over whether Sura 74:30 refers to nineteen angels or a general mathematical code. Dr. Khalifa asserts that Sura 72 contains no references to the Prophet Muhammad and points to mathematical patterns in the text discovered by Edip. Catherine continues with Sura 73, detailing the spiritual benefits of night meditation and the importance of choosing God as one's sole advocate. A discussion on self-defense and anger ensues, with contributions from Douglas, Hamid, and Robert on the ethics of fighting versus ignoring provocation. Dr. Khalifa emphasizes the absolute necessity of the Dawn (Fajr) prayer and explains that missing it is only excused under extreme circumstances like travel or exhaustive business. The session concludes with Dr. Khalifa announcing a new appendix on virginity and leading the group in reciting Al-Fatiha for several members' birthdays.

title: Quran Study 02 — Surah 95 & 96 — Quran Is Not Ink & Paper (Sabahi)
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa opens with a warning about Satan targeting believers on the straight path before introducing Dr. Mahmoud Sabahi to lead the study of Sura 95 (Al-Tin) and Sura 96 (Al-Alaq), assisted by Dan, Ali, and Amir. Sabahi categorizes twelve suras where God swears by natural phenomena and plants, prompting Khalifa to explain the symbolic connections between the fig (Adam), olive (Jesus), Mount Sinai (Moses), and Mecca (Abraham and Muhammad). Hamid and Khalifa detail botanical and nutritional aspects of figs and olive oil, including cholesterol reduction and alternate crop bearing. Khalifa uses a jar and human balance mechanisms to illustrate divine physical design in 95:4, while Sabahi and Dan discuss the spiritual descent into the "lowliest of the lowly" (95:5). Addressing a printing omission of verse 5, Khalifa presents mathematical evidence based on the number 19 to argue that the Quran's preservation rests in the heart rather than physical paper. Sabahi draws on his background in organic chemistry to explain plant molecular synthesis, anti-cancer compounds, and chemical chirality using a hand glove metaphor. Robert questions why God created human beings knowing most would choose Hell, which Khalifa answers by asserting that Earth serves as a second chance to nullify excuses. Turning to Sura 96, Sabahi outlines traditional accounts of Gabriel's first revelation to Muhammad, which Khalifa rejects as untrue. David, Lisa, Douglas, and Ali debate whether 'alaq in 96:2 should be translated as 'embryo' or 'clot,' with Khalifa citing Maurice Bucaille to reject 'clot.' Sabahi and Ali reflect on human transgression through wealth (96:6–7) and mandatory versus forbidden prayer, citing experiences in post-revolutionary Iran. Khalifa concludes with administrative updates and leads the recitation of Al-Fatiha.

title: Quran Study 03 — Surah 10:79-92 & 73 & 3:110-117 (Rashad)
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa leads a Friday gathering and study circle in Tucson, Arizona, opening with informal conversation alongside Ismail Barakat, Behrouz, and Mahmoud Abib regarding Iranian political culture and jokes about public grief versus private behavior. Khalifa recites Sura 10:79–92, drawing lessons on divine timing from the Red Sea crossing—rebutting a geologist's naturalistic explanation—and asserting that Pharaoh died a genuine believer whose late repentance failed to save his soul due to a lack of spiritual development. He shares anecdotes about the mummies at the Cairo Museum, a joke concerning Hosni Mubarak, and suspicions that a former acquaintance named Eric was a Saudi spy based on phone records. After reading Sura 23:1–14, Khalifa details the mathematical structure of the daily Contact Prayers (Salat) and discusses embryonic development stages described in verse 14. He and Mahmoud Abib present mathematical proofs centered on the occurrence of the word "God" in the Quran, including divisible verse totals, initialed sections, Abdullah's count of chapter and verse sums across 85 suras, and verse distances between 3:81 and 33:7 regarding the Messenger of the Covenant. In a sermon segment, Khalifa stresses prioritizing soul development through Salat over physical labor. Dr. Mahmoud Sabahi then leads a study of Sura 3:110–117, addressing social responsibilities, the dual covenants with God and society, historical lessons from Sura 2:60–61, and a CBS 60 Minutes report on drug addiction in Zurich to illustrate moral decline in affluent secular nations.

title: Quran Study 04 — Surah 37 & 3:118-129 — Asteroid (Rashad)
description: Shakira Karipineni, Ismail Barakat, Mahmoud Abib, and Dr. Rashad Khalifa begin with lighthearted conversation about cholesterol and newspaper allegations against Khalifa before turning to Sura 37 (Al-Saffat). Khalifa, Abib, and Barakat humorously categorize hypothetical methods disbelievers use to force their way into Hell—such as storming gates, tunneling under fences, pole vaulting, and hang gliding—to explain why heavenly residents feel no sadness for the damned. Khalifa and Karipineni share childhood memories of climbing high fences to sneak into Egyptian soccer matches and Indian grape orchards. Exegetical commentary covers Sura 37's descriptions of angels as "arrangers" and "blamers," the cosmological meaning of "Lord of the easts" (interpreted as the rising of planets and stars), creation from wet mud as evidence of divinely guided evolution, and the rejection of Lā Elāha Ella Allāh by arrogant leaders. Khalifa references a video critique by Bilal Philips and contrasts the Qur'anic Shahada (3:18) with traditional Sunni formulas. Following readings of Sura 10:43–54, Abib shares a news report on H. Jay Melosh's theory regarding asteroid impacts and global firestorms, which Khalifa connects to the smoke prophesied in Sura 44. Dr. Mahmoud Sabahi leads a study of Sura 3:118–129, analyzing the psychological state of hypocrites who bite their fingers in rage, a habit cross-referenced by Douglas to Sura 25:27. Commentary from Edip Yüksel, Abdullah, and Khalifa stresses severing close ties with hostile outsiders before Sabahi and Khalifa conclude with the historical context of the Battle of Badr and divine angelic assistance.

title: Quran Study 05 — Surah 56:75 & 57 (Lisa)
description: Lisa opens the study of Sura 56, verse 75, emphasizing the vast scale of the universe by citing galaxy counts, light-year distances across the Milky Way, and Psalm 8:3–4 to illustrate the gravity of God swearing by the positions of the stars. Reading verses 77 through 80, she contends that the phrase stating none can touch the Quran except the righteous refers to spiritual understanding and the discovery of its mathematical miracle. Addressing an audience question regarding the word "touch," Dr. Rashad Khalifa reads the study footnote to reject traditional ablution rules as a satanic plot, asserting that comprehension is granted exclusively by God. Khalifa hands out a summary sheet of the 19-based miracle, listing contributors such as Abdullah, Mahmood, Ihsan, Lisa, Feroz, Ismail, and Gatut, and demonstrates multi-thousand-digit numbers derived from verse and sura counts. Responding to Farhad Mo'ini's inquiry on number divisibility and a caller from Louisville, Kentucky, Khalifa argues that every Quranic verse is divine except two verses in Sura 9. Turning to verses 88 through 96, Lisa describes the allegorical nature of High Heaven, Lower Heaven, and Hell. Khalifa maintains that those who die before age 40, citing Malcolm X and Martin Luther King Jr., are granted Lower Heaven by divine mercy, drawing parallels to Abraham's understanding and Joseph's protection from sin in Sura 12:24. In Q&A, Catherine asks about generations of believers, and Hussein asks about age forty. Moving to Sura 57:1–5, Lisa discusses divine control over all matter and human hearts, before a group of children and a woman perform a devotional song on remembering God.

title: Quran Study 06 — Surah 59 — PRA, Invisible Giants, Hypocrites (Donna)
description: Donna opens a study circle session on Sura 59, discussing verses 5 through 10 regarding divine control over disbelievers' actions, angelic protection, and the equitable distribution of war spoils to prevent monopolization by the rich, which she compares to Hitler's plunder in World War II. Dr. Rashad Khalifa elaborates on verse 6, asserting that believers are accompanied by invisible angelic guardians and presenting local community events—including emergency financial aid collected for Emily and Lori surviving a rollover car crash unharmed—as empirical evidence. Donna and Dr. Khalifa address Sura 59:7–10, condemning sectarian abuses of verse 7 by Sunni and Shia sects while citing Sura 6:159 and Sura 3:103 to stress believer unity. Following audience questions regarding hypocrites, Dr. Khalifa defines hypocrisy as ego-worship and an inability to utter the shahada without adding Muhammad, referencing Sura 39:45 and Sura 4 while discussing political repression in Iran alongside Hamid and Parivash Ettefagh. Continuing with Sura 59:18–20, Donna discusses daily soul-nourishment, leading Dr. Khalifa to frame righteous deeds as deposits into a "Post Retirement Account" (PRA) for eternity, contrasting medical school preparation with eternal life. Reviewing Sura 59:21–24, Donna and Dr. Khalifa discuss the awesomeness of the Quran and divine attributes, supported by Abdullah's observations on mathematical coding, Dr. Khalifa's reflection on human physical design, Robert's inquiry on hypocrites citing Sura 12:103, and Farhad Mo'ini's questions about Quranic compilation history and Sura 53. The session ends with a group recitation of Sura 1 (Al-Fatiha) for Matt's birthday.

title: Quran Study 07 — Surah 62 & 63 — God's Religion Will Dominate (Catherine)
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa opens the session with a significant announcement regarding the upcoming publication of a new, purified Quran translation, which he intends to release during Ramadan. He explains the historical corruption of the Quranic text, asserting that the original chronological order was altered by the Umayyads to include two verses in Sura 9 that idolize the Prophet Muhammad. He argues that this corruption, alongside the distortion of religious practices like the Azan and the ritual prayer, resulted in the loss of the pure Quran for centuries. Following this, Kathryn leads a study of Sura 62 and 63, focusing on the nature of God’s unlimited grace and the metaphor of the donkey carrying books to describe those who possess scripture but fail to understand it. The group discusses the concept of being "God's chosen," with Dr. Khalifa clarifying that this status is not an exclusive guarantee of salvation but a responsibility that many have distorted through arrogance. The conversation shifts to the importance of the Friday Prayer, which Dr. Khalifa emphasizes as a divine commandment that transcends cultural or gender-based restrictions often imposed by Hadith. The session concludes with a discussion on the hypocrites described in Sura 63, the nature of intercession, and the group reciting Al-Fatiha for various personal requests, including academic success for community members and the continued presence of a guest.

title: Quran Study 08 — Surah 65 & 66 — Enjoin Kids To Do Salat, Hamid Argues (Lori)
description: Lori leads a study of Sura 65 (Al-Talaq, 10–12) and Sura 66 (Al-Tahreem, 1–12), analyzing human creation, marital duties, and prophetic fallibility. Discussing 65:10–11, she explains that humans possess sufficient intelligence to believe rather than totally disbelieving like jinns, and that messengers serve to lead existing believers out of darkness. Dr. Rashad Khalifa addresses divorce laws, explaining alimony provisions and nursing mother allowances in 65:6–7. He argues that evolution within species is a divinely guided scientific fact, contrasting it with Darwinian natural selection and atheist evolution. He asserts that six other uninhabited Earths exist to prove on the Day of Judgment that life did not randomly evolve from chemical conditions. After an unedited manuscript typo found by Poopak is addressed, a participant questions how divorce arbitration functions in practice; Dr. Khalifa states that Quranic guidelines rely on conscience and mutual consultation. Transitioning to 66:1–7, Lori highlights Muhammad's human fallibility and the rejection of prophetic idolization. Hamid raises concerns regarding how far parents should force children to observe Salat, prompting Dr. Khalifa and Lori to cite 20:132 on persistent exhortation without compulsion. Beth offers personal testimony about her upbringing, noting that forcing children breeds resentment. Concluding with 66:8–12, Lori discusses sincere repentance, the struggle against hypocrites, and how the wives of Noah, Lot, Pharaoh, and Mary disprove the doctrine of intercession. The session ends with two recitations of Al-Fatiha for group members.

title: Quran Study 09 — Surah 70 — Chastity, Worry, Edip's Translation Request (Edip)
description: Edip Yuksel leads a study of Sura 70 (Al-Ma'arij), opening with Dr. Rashad Khalifa citing Sura 26 regarding reading the Quran in non-native languages. Edip discusses the relativity of time in 70:4, comparing human standards of age to flies and dogs—prompted by Lydia—while Khalifa references Carl Sagan's novel and Einstein's relativity theory to explain light speed and Prophet Muhammad's ascension. Examining 70:19–34, Edip addresses the passive creation of human anxiety, while Khalifa recounts an anecdote about his father's teacher debating mullahs over worry and despondency. Khalifa presents 70:29 as a command for chastity, citing a Joe Sobran column on sexual consequences and health risks like AIDS and cervical cancer mentioned by Naghmeh, while contrasting university condom giveaways with parental duties. On 70:30, Khalifa argues that "what is legally theirs" includes common law and non-traditional marital arrangements, responding to queries from Farhad Mo'ini, Parivash Ettefagh, and Douglas. Edip shares a personal story of a Turkish printing mix-up between 29:45 and 39:45 after neglecting his contact prayers. Dr. Mahmoud Sabahi, Robert, Martha, and Naghmeh ask questions regarding marital obligations, wealth as a virtue via Sura 16, verse order preservation through Gabriel, the historical Umayyad conflict following Uthman's era, and Behruz Mofidi Shirazi's Farsi translation project.

title: Quran Study 10 — Surah 71 & 72 — Chastity, Jinns (Apamea)
description: Apamea Bashar leads the study of Sura 71 (Noah) and Sura 72 (Al-Jinn) on May 19, 1989. After Apamea recites Sura 71, she reflects on Noah's 950-year ministry, verse 71:17 comparing human growth to plant germination, and the pre-Islamic idols in 71:23. Dr. Rashad Khalifa compares Noah's struggles in 71:7 to a law student's rejection of mathematical Quranic proofs related by Naghmeh, and uses dead insects trapped in a light fixture outside the Tucson mosque as an allegory for sinners seeking damnation. Khalifa identifies the Dead Sea as a remnant of Noah's flood, highlights the scientific distinction between the sun's direct light and the moon's reflective surface in 71:16—citing Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin—and argues from 71:25 that souls learn their ultimate fate at death. Moving to Sura 72, Apamea reads verses 1–18, touching on jinn seeking power through witchery and devil worship. Khalifa asserts Sura 72 prophesies events at Masjid Tucson, pointing to four occurrences of the root Rashada and 19-based gematria. He explains jinn mechanics, claiming they travel light-years and referencing a 76-second space shuttle launch abort. Khalifa interrupts to instruct youth attendee Amir on chastity, defining it as abstaining from premarital contact. In a debate over 72:18, Rami, Edip, and Dr. Mahmoud Sabahi question whether prohibiting names beside God's applies strictly to Contact Prayer or to physical mosque premises, while Khalifa argues for dedicated prayer spaces free of non-divine names.

title: Quran Study 11 — Surah 23:60-88 & 16 (Behrouz)
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa hosts a morning study session in Tucson, Arizona, opening with commentary on international news regarding political revolts against Mikhail Gorbachev in Moscow and Nicolae Ceaușescu in Romania. Reading Sura 23:60–88, he equates the "Zikr" (reminder) in verse 71 to the Quran's mathematical code and addresses disbelievers who reject resurrection, mentioning Susan Rey's belief that Ali, Hussein, and Fatima will return. He references Beirut as a center of moral corruption punished by God before leading a recitation of Al-Fatiha for a participant named Soad. Reading Sura 16:66–72, Khalifa elaborates on bee hive social hierarchy, worker scouts calculating flight angles and distances, pollen leg pockets, and honey's ability to cure local allergies. Turning to Sura 11:38–60, he discusses Noah building the ark, referencing a joke by Bill Cosby, and asserts that God maintains total control over every individual creature, using AIDS as an example of targeted divine retribution. After reciting Sura 10:26–34, he describes Hell as absolute darkness and explains that saint worship at tombs constitutes imploring nothingness. He shares personal anecdotes about an elderly man with hearing loss seen on his twenty-seventh wedding anniversary and a participant's eye surgery, concluding with a discussion on genetics, DNA, and James Watson.

title: Quran Study 12 — Behrouz's Sermon & Edip's Exposure (Behrouz)
description: Behrouz delivers a Friday Khutba addressing congregational decorum and reverence for God's messenger, Dr. Rashad Khalifa, following a visitor's concern over how Khalifa was treated. Citing numerous verses including 6:8–9, 49:1–5, and 24:62, Behrouz argues that believers must refrain from arguing with the messenger, raising their voices, or addressing him by his first name during official sessions, drawing comparisons to President Bush and citing Sammy Khalifa's conduct. Following prayer, Dr. Mahmoud Sabahi objects to Behrouz's tone, comparing it to rigid religious establishments. During the subsequent Quran study, Khalifa addresses human rebelliousness using the parable of the heifer in Sura 2 and recent dress-code breaches under 7:31, prompting commentary from Laurie, Linda Baroni, and others on modesty. Edip Yuksel defends himself against claims of ego worship, citing his sacrifices in Turkey and quoting 2:269, 17:36, 49:12, 24:63, 60:12, and 3:159 to argue that obedience is conditional and discussion is permitted. A heated debate ensues regarding past discussions on God's omnipotence and whether God operates through angels, during which Edip accuses Behrouz of claiming God did not create hydrogen. Khalifa, Ahmad, and Martha explain God's physical system of using angels (3:59, 15:29, 21:91), warning that raising opinions above the messenger nullifies good works (49:2). Dr. Mahmoud Sabahi recites Sura 114 and 3:103–106 appealing for unity, while Ali defends Edip's right to speak. Khalifa cautions Edip against idolizing his opinion (39:65). Douglas quotes 39:18 and 58:10 on Satanic division, after which Khalifa leads recitation of Al-Fatiha. Apamea Bashar concludes by teaching 3:130–132 and 2:275 on usury.

title: Quran Study 13 — Surah 7:12 — Adam & Eve's Bodies (Rashad)
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa leads a study of Sura 7 (Al-A'raf), verses 12 through 27, examining Satan's refusal to prostrate, his dismissal from God's kingdom, and his request for respite to lead humans astray. Khalifa argues that Satan's rebellion demonstrates free choice among creatures and asserts that opponents of God's physical evidence in the Quran use falsehood to combat truth, citing 40:5. Study participants Atif, Ihsan Ramadan, and Edip Yüksel discuss a conference where a scholar argued the Quran was hallucinated by Muhammad and where a critic objected to numeric counts over geminate letters (shaddas). Khalifa and Ihsan recount an incident where Ihsan experienced a separation of soul and body during a hospitalization, perceiving a large figure identified as Abraham. This prompts a detailed discussion on the nature of Adam and Eve's bodies in Paradise, verse 7:22, whether their physical forms were in Heaven or on Earth, and how souls are assigned to bodies. Parivash Ettefagh shares a dream about the Shahada and verse 7:172, arguing that human souls bore witness to God's lordship prior to earthly existence, making "Ash-hadu Alla Elaha Ella Allah" an eyewitness testimony. The group reads 38:67-76 regarding the High Society feud and 67:2 on the creation of death and life. Atif relates a clinical out-of-body experience during dental surgery, leading Khalifa to discuss Jesus's crucifixion, the distinction between body, spirit, and soul, and his own scientific publication on carrot cloning in Nature. The conversation concludes with remarks on Stephen Hawking and the fine-tuned expansion of the universe.

title: Quran Study 14 — Night of Destiny Zikr (Rashad)
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa leads a zikr session on the Night of Destiny (Laylat al-Qadr), framing spiritual growth as the transition of the soul from infancy to adulthood through the commemoration of God. He argues that while creation glorifies God by necessity, humans exercise free choice, asserting that those who neglect zikr are characterized in the Quran as unjust and ignorant. Khalifa describes how repeating the divine name wipes out past sins and deposits spiritual capital into a Post-Retirement Account for eternity, citing twenty-three Quranic passages that promise health, wealth, and dignity to those who remember God. Discussing the unseen realm, he presents the angels on this night as actively descending to assist believers with personal matters, including health issues and job or immigration applications. He references Sura Al-Qadr, Sura 1 (Al-Fatiha), and Sura 2:186 regarding God's response to prayer. Throughout the gathering, he directs communal chanting of La Elaha Ella Allah and Qayyum, maintaining that expanded souls love and overlap across great distances while stunted souls remain trapped in conflict.

title: Quran Study 15 — Surah 54:23 & 55-56 & 51 — Age 40 & First Gen. (Rashad)
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa leads a study of Sura 54 (verses 23–40), arguing that AIDS represents divine retribution for homosexuality and discussing media warnings directed at the Arab world. Martha questions his translation of Sura 54:37, prompting a discussion on using "incurred" rather than "deserved" retribution. Khalifa mentions a 12,692-digit number compiled by Abdullah as a multiple of 19 and criticizes Islamic centers for aligning with Catholic censorship regarding Salman Rushdie. Lori presents Sura 55, leading Khalifa to describe jinns as beings of fire moving faster than light. Discussing Sura 56, he designates those enduring ridicule for upholding God alone as the "first generation" destined for the highest heaven. He reasserts that individuals who die before age 40, including Martin Luther King Jr. and Malcolm X, automatically enter the Lower Heaven to protect them from environmental corruption. Lisa reads Sura 57:4–5 on divine control, while Douglas Brown introduces Sura 51. Khalifa illustrates God's creation using atmospheric oxygen levels—referencing the 1967 Apollo 1 fire—and argues from Genesis 22 that Ishmael, not Isaac, was Abraham's sacrificed son.

title: Quran Study 16 — Surah 64 & 59 & 70 — Nothing Happens & Angels Are The Best Surgeons (Rashad)
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa introduces the page layout of his forthcoming Quran translation, demonstrating the mathematical coding of the word God (2,698 occurrences, multiple of 19) to verify divine authorship. Analyzing Sura 64:1-9, he argues that divine omnipotence guarantees perfect happiness for believers, comparing God's warranty to commercial guarantees by Lee Iacocca, while rejecting Bukhari hadith claiming righteous people suffer most. Addressing Sura 10:62, he asserts that physical afflictions, such as Rabbi Kushner's son suffering from progeria, stem from Satanic harm when divine protection is forfeited. He explains two fundamental divine laws: that nothing happens except by God's will, and nothing occurs except as a consequence of human actions, citing his nephew's missed Morning Prayers in Egypt and Douglas's sermon on morning light exposure curing depression. Edip Yüksel presents a study of Sura 70:15-34, analyzing the passive grammatical structure of kholiqa in verse 19 to argue humans create their own anxiety rather than God creating flawed designs. Edip and Khalifa address Sura 70:30, clarifying that "what is legally theirs" encompasses common-law and cultural marriage practices. Following a quote from Joe Sobran on casual sex, Khalifa outlines an upcoming appendix on youth chastity. Further Q&A features Dr. Mahmoud Sabahi, Farhad Mo'ini, Parivash Ettefagh, and Martha, touching upon arranged marriages, Farsi translations by Behrooz Shirazi, textual additions under Caliph Uthman, and the spiritual mechanism of Gabriel's revelation to Prophet Muhammad.

title: Quran Study 17 — Surah 82-83 & 90-91 (Rashad)
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa opens with informal mosque updates, welcoming back Muhtesem Erisen and offering advice on hand placement during Prayer before leading a study of Surah 90 (Al-Balad). He posits that human gestation (266 days) and bird egg incubation reflect mathematical multiples of seven and nineteen, and interprets the difficult path of verse 4 as hard work required to redeem the soul from its original rebellion in High Society. Emphasizing the daily prayers, he warns against idolizing money and cites Surah 29:17, read by Lydia, to assert God as sole provider. He illustrates divine design using the mechanics of human eyes and tongues, contrasting the narrow path of worship with widespread idol worship. A debate on verse 4 ensues when Dr. Mahmoud Sabahi brings up a Farsi translation rendering kabad as pain and suffering; Dr. Khalifa counters that believers do not suffer continuous misery. Turning to Surah 91 (Al-Shams), Dr. Khalifa cites planetary precision and California redwoods as evidence of divine creation, contrasting scientific astronomical data with traditional moon-sighting practices. Following birthday prayers for Sarah and Alia, Edip Yuksel presents Surah 82 and Surah 83, analyzing mathematical counts of the word Allah and discussing the translation of Yawm al-Din. Edip and Dr. Khalifa argue that the numerically structured book (Sijjeen and Elleyyeen) refers to the Quran itself, which the righteous witness while disbelievers dismiss as tales of the past.

title: Quran Study 18 — Surah 61 & 87 & 94 & 81 (Rashad)
description: In this study circle, Dr. Rashad Khalifa and Edip Yuksel analyze several suras of the Quran, focusing on the mathematical structure and the practical implications of the text. Dr. Khalifa explains the testing process for women during wartime described in Sura 60, emphasizing that believers must pledge to worship God alone and avoid sinful behavior, while cautioning that not all orders from a prophet are binding unless they are righteous. The group discusses the mathematical miracle of the number 19, which Dr. Khalifa argues will lead to the global prevalence of Islam within 50 years. The study shifts to Sura 87, where the group explores God's design in nature, specifically the camel's biological adaptations, which they present as evidence of divine creation. The discussion progresses to Sura 88, detailing the apocalyptic events of the Day of Judgment, including the implosion of the universe. The participants also examine Sura 89, reflecting on the historical destruction of 'Ad and Thamud as divine retribution for arrogance and the mistreatment of the poor. Throughout the recording, Dr. Khalifa addresses the oppression of women in contemporary Saudi Arabia and Iran, characterizing forced veiling and the denial of rights as modern forms of burying girls alive. The session concludes with an examination of Sura 81 and the role of the Messenger of the Covenant, with Dr. Khalifa sharing personal accounts of his spiritual experiences and the mathematical proofs connecting his name to the Quranic text.

title: Quran Study 19 — Surah 2:89 — Witchcraft, Reverting, Intro To Blue Quran (Edip)
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa leads a study circle through a detailed examination of Sura 2:89–119, focusing on the historical and spiritual patterns of disbelief among those who claim to be recipients of scripture. He emphasizes the role of the ego in rejecting God's messengers, drawing parallels between the historical rejection of Moses and Jesus by their respective communities and the contemporary resistance to the mathematical miracle of the Quran. He discusses the nature of witchcraft, attributing it to the influence of jinns and explaining it as a test of faith, while cautioning that such practices are ultimately futile against God's will. Throughout the session, he highlights the importance of the Contact Prayers (Salat) and the necessity of absolute devotion to God alone, warning that those who disregard these commandments or succumb to jealousy will face severe consequences. The discussion also touches on the divine nature of the Quran's structure and the significance of the mathematical code 19, which he presents as a sign of God's omnipotence and a means of refining the believers.

title: Quran Study 20 — Surah 3 — Insurance, Worry, Fear (Sabahi)
description: Dr. Mahmoud Sabahi leads a study circle in Tucson, Arizona, focusing on the opening verses of Sura 3. He examines the nature of straightforward versus multiple-meaning verses, arguing that those who harbor doubt in their hearts deliberately exploit allegorical passages to create confusion, a tactic he claims is prevalent among traditional scholars who prioritize sectarian interpretation over the essence of the Quran. Dr. Sabahi and Dr. Rashad Khalifa discuss the role of those who possess knowledge, asserting that true understanding is accessible to any seeker of truth rather than a privileged clerical class. The group analyzes the significance of the phrase "there is no god except He" and the importance of maintaining absolute belief in God without the distraction of worldly concerns like insurance or fear of the future. Dr. Khalifa emphasizes that believers are prisoners of war in a temporary world, and he characterizes the material pleasures described in Sura 3:14 as mere vanities compared to the eternal abode. The session concludes with a discussion on the responsibility of believers to deliver the message of submission, with participants sharing personal experiences of proselytizing and the shift toward using the term "submitter" to avoid the prejudices associated with the word "Muslim" in contemporary political contexts.

title: Quran Study 21 — Surah 9:52 & 56:75 — The Hypocrites (Rashad)
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa leads a study circle session focused on Sura 9:52-68 and Sura 56:75-96. He begins by explicating the hypocrites' response to the messenger, arguing that their performance of Salat was tainted by laziness and disbelief, serving as evidence that the contact prayers existed prior to the Quran. He discusses the distribution of charity, emphasizing that Zakat must prioritize poor relatives, and warns against the divisive nature of hypocrites who masquerade as believers. Following a discussion on the importance of documenting loans, Lisa presents an analysis of Sura 56:75, reflecting on the vastness of the universe and the mathematical miracle of the Quran. Dr. Khalifa elaborates on the number 19, detailing recent discoveries regarding the Quran's numerical structure and asserting that only the righteous are permitted to uncover these proofs. The session concludes with a reading of the final verses of Sura 56, which categorize souls into the Highest Heaven, the Lower Heaven, and Hell, with Lisa emphasizing the allegorical nature of these descriptions and the necessity of glorifying God.

title: Quran Study 22 — Surah 39:11 & 37:164 & 28 — Admission Test, No Insurance Compromise (Rashad)
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa leads a study circle focusing on the profound implications of Sura 39:11-14, emphasizing the absolute necessity of worshiping God alone and the transformative nature of being an "utmost submitter." He argues that a true submitter experiences a perfect life free from problems, attributing any personal hardship to one's own failure to follow God's law or a necessary "admission test" designed to purge human defects. Throughout the session, he shares personal anecdotes, including his recent experiences with his wife and the peaceful resolution of potential conflicts, to illustrate how God manipulates hearts to protect those who trust Him. The discussion extends to the nature of Satan, the role of the jinn companion, and the interpretation of Sura 37:159-182 and Sura 38:1-16, where he explains the mathematical code of the Quran and the inevitable retribution awaiting those who reject the message. Participants engage in a lively Q&A, questioning the nature of jinn, the validity of astrology, and the historical context of specific verses, while Dr. Khalifa consistently redirects them to the Quran's clear guidance and the importance of avoiding the worship of ancestors or religious figures.

title: Quran Study 23 — Surah 51 — New Era, Believers Protected From Accidents & Diseases (Douglas)
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa leads a Quranic study session in Tucson, Arizona, with Douglas Brown serving as the primary speaker for the analysis of Sura 51. The discussion begins with an examination of the opening verses of Sura 51, which describe the winds and clouds as divine mechanisms for distributing bounty, with Dr. Khalifa drawing an analogy between these natural systems and the life-support requirements for astronauts in space. Douglas argues that the Quranic code provides irrefutable proof of God's existence and the timing of the Day of Judgment, asserting that deviators reject these signs because they are predestined to do so. The group explores the narrative of Abraham and his angelic guests, discussing the birth of Isaac and the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah. Dr. Khalifa clarifies the distinction between Ishmael and Isaac, rejecting biblical accounts that he characterizes as racial distortions. The session concludes with a debate regarding divine protection, where Dr. Khalifa maintains that sincere believers are shielded from worldly disasters, including diseases and accidents, while acknowledging that death remains an inevitable transition for all human beings.

title: Quran Study 24 — Surah 55 & 56 (Lori)
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa and his study circle in Tucson, Arizona, examine Sura 55 and 56, focusing on the nature of Heaven, Hell, and the spiritual development of the soul. Dr. Khalifa begins by addressing the community, clarifying his previous remarks regarding the "best" cake-makers to emphasize that every believer is special. Laurie leads the study of Sura 55, highlighting the distinction between the Higher Heaven and the Lower Heaven, and the role of jinns as companions who share the same requirements for salvation as humans. The group discusses the concept of original sin, the necessity of the five daily prayers as sustenance for the soul, and the visual manifestation of spiritual development in the Hereafter. Dr. Khalifa explains that the guilty will be recognizable by their deformed, shrunken appearance, while the righteous will be rewarded with proximity to God. Naghmeh continues the study with Sura 56, discussing the "far ahead" believers who are closest to God, and the distinction between the early generations of believers and later ones. The participants share anecdotes about facing ridicule and persecution for their commitment to worshipping God alone, drawing parallels to the experiences of Noah and Abraham. Dr. Khalifa emphasizes that their current generation is a "first generation" of believers who are restoring the true message of Islam, and he presents mathematical evidence from the Quran as a sign of its divine origin. The session concludes with a discussion on the inevitability of the Day of Judgment and the graphic descriptions of Hell for those who reject the truth.

title: Quran Study 25 — Surah 58 (Robert)
description: Robert leads a study session on Sura 58, "The Debate," focusing on the Quranic laws regarding the estrangement of wives and the expiation required for such actions. He reads verses 58:1-9, emphasizing God's omniscience and the prohibition of secret conspiracies that foster disharmony. Dr. Rashad Khalifa joins the discussion, explaining the historical context of the "mother" analogy used by husbands to punish wives and detailing the Quranic solutions for reconciliation, including freeing a slave or fasting. The group examines the mathematical nature of the Quran, noting that Sura 58 mentions God in every verse. Dr. Khalifa and other attendees share anecdotes about past troublemakers who attempted to divide the study circle, framing these events as tests of faith. The session continues with verses 58:10-22, covering the importance of making room for others, the necessity of charity, and the requirement to prioritize God over family ties. A new attendee, Keikhosrow Emami, shares his personal journey of discovering the Quranic message in the United States, his transition to the study circle, and his commitment to the Contact Prayer.

title: Quran Study 26 — Surah 67 — Hamid Argues With Rashad (Gatut)
description: Gatut Adisoma leads a study session on Sura 67, Al-Mulk, focusing on the nature of God's sovereignty, the purpose of human existence, and the flawless design of the universe. He explains that God grants kingship to believers, who are liberated from the worldly anxieties associated with celebrity and material wealth. Adisoma discusses the creation of seven universes, identifying the innermost as a prison for Satan, and highlights the Quranic warnings regarding Hell, where disbelievers will eventually confess their denial of God's revelations. Dr. Rashad Khalifa interjects to emphasize the precision of God's system, citing the predictable movements of celestial bodies and the moon's synchronized rotation. The session transitions into a contentious debate between Hamid, Dr. Khalifa, and other attendees regarding the extent of God's daily interference in human affairs. Hamid argues that humans possess individual agency and that God does not intervene in mundane choices, a view Dr. Khalifa and other students challenge by asserting that God controls every aspect of existence, including human speech and actions. The discussion concludes with a recitation of Al-Fatiha for community members and a preview of the next session.

title: Quran Study 27 — Surah 14:18 & 17:47 — Chastity, Salat As A Gift, DOJ, Quran Traps (Eric)
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa leads a study circle in Tucson, Arizona, focusing on the interpretation of Sura 14, verses 19 through 33, while addressing broader theological questions regarding the upbringing of children and the nature of belief. He emphasizes the Quranic teaching that God created the heavens and the earth for a specific purpose and argues that the past tense used in prophetic descriptions of the Day of Judgment signifies events that are certain to occur. A significant portion of the session involves a heated exchange with an attendee named Eric regarding the necessity of formal schooling and the proper method for disciplining children. Dr. Khalifa strongly rejects the use of physical punishment, characterizing it as a satanic practice that alienates children from religious teachings. He also discusses the role of parents in setting a righteous example, citing the importance of teaching children to perform Salat at home. The discussion shifts to the nature of the Quran as the sole source of wisdom, with Dr. Khalifa critiquing the reliance on Hadith and illustrating the dangers of sectarian practices, such as temporary marriages performed near the Ka‘bah. He concludes by clarifying the nature of resurrection, correcting the translation of "dead" to "unconscious" in Sura 39:68, and reiterating that for God, there is no time sequence in creation.

title: Quran Study 28 — Surah 45:33 — 19 Math (Edip)
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa leads a study circle in Tucson, Arizona, focusing on the mathematical structure of the Quran and the rejection of sectarian idolatry. He opens by discussing Sura 45:33-37 and 46:1-14, emphasizing that idolators will eventually be disowned by the very figures they worship, such as Muhammad or Ali, on the Day of Judgment. Khalifa highlights the mathematical miracle of the Quran, specifically the number 19, which he argues serves as God's signature and a physical proof of the scripture's integrity. He recounts the historical discovery of this code by Rabbi Judah the Pious, whom he identifies as the witness mentioned in 46:10. The discussion shifts to the origins of human existence, with Khalifa explaining that humans were originally in God's kingdom before being sent to Earth to choose between God's message and Satan's. Participants share personal anecdotes about their transition to monotheism and the absurdity of traditional religious rituals, such as specific rules for cutting nails or entering restrooms, which they characterize as sectarian fabrications designed to monopolize religious authority. The session concludes with a critique of the sectarian divisions in prayer leadership, contrasting the simplicity of Quranic submission with the complex, man-made requirements prevalent in Sunni and Shia traditions.

title: Quran Study 29 — 1985 Tucson, Mehri's Questions, Admission Test & Final Test (Parivash)
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa leads a study circle in Tucson, Arizona, in 1985, focusing on the theological implications of Sura 29 and the nature of human testing. He addresses questions regarding the Fitrat, or innate human instinct to recognize God, and argues that individuals cannot plead ignorance or blame their parents for their religious choices. The discussion pivots to the story of Iblis, whom Khalifa describes as having been exposed by God for his refusal to prostrate before Adam, a rebellion rooted in his desire to rule a portion of God's kingdom. Khalifa critiques the tendency of religious groups, specifically citing Sheikh Metwalli Sha'rawi, to associate other names with God, which he classifies as the unforgivable sin of Shirk. He also recounts the story of a young woman named Jennifer, using her tragic accident to illustrate the chaos caused by Satan when individuals step outside of God's protection. The session includes a Q&A segment where participants ask about the necessity of ablution, the nature of prayer, and why the Quran repeats certain messages across different suras.

title: Quran Study 30 — Surah 28 & 57 & 45:33 — Insurance, Rashad Told To Devote All Time To God (Edip)
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa explores the divine law of God supporting the oppressed through the history of the children of Israel in Egypt, specifically focusing on the narrative of Moses in Sura 28. He details the birth of Moses, his mother's reliance on God's guidance, and his eventual adoption by Pharaoh's family, characterizing Pharaoh's wife as a secret believer planted by God. The discussion shifts to Moses' accidental killing of an Egyptian, which Dr. Khalifa frames as a divinely orchestrated event that prepared Moses for his future leadership. The session transitions to Sura 57, where Dr. Khalifa discusses the deterioration of religion, the nature of worldly life as a temporary illusion, and the importance of believing in God and His messengers. He shares a personal anecdote about his own experience of 'righteous death' while listening to Quranic recitation, and recounts a specific incident in Phoenix where a file regarding his own accident served as a sign to his coworkers. The session concludes with a detailed examination of the mathematical miracle of the Quran, specifically the significance of the number 19, and a theological explanation of the origin of human souls as former angels who were given a second chance to choose between God and Satan.

title: Quran Study 31 — Surah 18:98 & 81 — Azan & Salat (Rashad)
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa leads a study circle in Tucson, Arizona, focusing on the interpretation of Sura 18:98-110 and Sura 81, while addressing the mathematical miracle of the Quran. He discusses the prophecy of Gog and Magog, arguing that their emergence is linked to the year 2271 and a 17-century timeline from the revelation of the Quran. Khalifa asserts that 'Zikr' refers specifically to the Quran's mathematical code, which serves as a divine guarantee of the scripture's preservation. The session includes a detailed critique of traditional religious practices, specifically criticizing the inclusion of names other than God in the Shahada and the addition of non-Quranic steps to the Wudu and Salat. Khalifa and his student Edip analyze the end-of-the-world imagery in Sura 81, describing the cosmic events as a divine implosion. The discussion touches upon the oppression of women in certain Muslim-majority cultures, which Khalifa characterizes as a modern form of burying daughters alive. He also shares personal anecdotes regarding his experiences as God's Messenger of the Covenant, explaining his summons to the high horizon and the confirmation of his mission by the prophets. The recording concludes with reflections on the fortunate nature of the current generation in receiving these divine signs.

title: Quran Study 32 — Surah 22:15 — Which Masjids To Pray In (Vicky)
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa leads a study circle in Tucson, Arizona, where he addresses the interpretation of Sura 22:15, critiquing traditional translations that suggest a believer should commit suicide if they doubt God's support. Khalifa and his students, including Edip, analyze how various commentators like Maududi have mistranslated the verse, arguing instead that the passage commands the believer to sever dependencies on others and rely solely on God. The discussion shifts to the physical expansion of their mosque, with Khalifa noting that they have outgrown their current space and planning further growth. He expresses skepticism regarding other local mosques, specifically citing incorrect Qibla orientation in a nearby facility. Parivash Ettefagh raises a question about the prohibition of praying in mosques that do not uphold the Quranic message, leading the group to reference Sura 9:108 as a strict commandment against such practices. The session concludes with anecdotal accounts from Vicky and others regarding children and individuals reciting Zikr, such as 'Allah' or the Shahada, during their sleep or at moments of waking, which Khalifa interprets as evidence of the subconscious mind being naturally attuned to the worship of God.

title: Quran Study 33 — Surah 74 (Sabahi)
description: Dr. Mahmoud Sabahi leads a study circle session on Sura 74, examining the text through the lens of the Quranic mathematical code. He argues that the opening verses, traditionally interpreted as instructions to Muhammad, serve as universal guidance for believers to cleanse their message of centuries of corruption. Sabahi analyzes the description of the disbeliever who is provided with wealth and children yet remains greedy, positing that true richness is found only in contentment with God. He reflects on his personal journey from a religious upbringing in Iran to his eventual arrival in Tucson, where he encountered the message of worshipping God alone. The discussion shifts to the significance of the number 19, which Sabahi and Dr. Rashad Khalifa present as a divine mechanism to strengthen the faith of believers and expose those harboring doubt. Participants debate the nature of multi-meaning words in the Quran, with Edip arguing that traditional interpretations often force human traditions onto the text. Sabahi concludes by emphasizing that intercession is non-existent and that the Quran serves as a reminder for those who wish to take heed, while noting that the presence of hypocrites is a sign of a message gaining strength.

title: Quran Study 34 — Surah 33 — God Is Physical Innovations/Praying & Prostrating After Salat (Chester)
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa leads a study circle discussion focused on Sura 33 of the Quran, emphasizing the necessity of maintaining a strictly numerical and Quranic approach to prayer and worship. He warns against the introduction of innovations, such as performing additional prostrations after the final salutation, which he argues disrupts the numerical structure of Salat. The discussion transitions into an analysis of Sura 33:1-7, where Dr. Khalifa addresses the prophet Muhammad's role as an example for believers and refutes accusations of idol worship directed at his followers. He clarifies that the covenant mentioned in 33:7 is the same one detailed in 3:81, involving all prophets, and asserts that Muhammad was a participant in this pledge to support the Messenger of the Covenant. The session includes an extensive dialogue regarding the physical nature of God, with Dr. Khalifa utilizing astronomical concepts to illustrate the vastness of the seven universes and God's physical presence. He rejects the notion that God is merely a spirit, arguing instead that God is the most physical of all entities, and discusses the state of the soul after death, distinguishing between the experiences of believers and disbelievers. Participants engage in a debate about the nature of God's physical manifestation and the paradoxes of creation, while Dr. Khalifa insists that all religious understanding must be derived solely from the Quran.

title: Quran Study 35 — Rashad Makes Deliberate Mistakes To Destroy idols (Ismail)
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa leads a study circle focusing on Sura 30:25-32, emphasizing the natural instinct of monotheism and the absurdity of idolatry. He discusses the concept of Satan's incompetence, arguing that the existence of suffering, such as starving children, is a demonstration of Satan's inability to manage his own dominion, and that these victims are ultimately redeemed by God's mercy. Dr. Khalifa recounts his personal history working at Anheuser-Busch, where he developed a patented process for extracting protein from brewer's yeast, which he presents as a miracle that emerged from the heart of a major alcohol manufacturing center. He explains that the mathematical miracle of the Quran was hidden in plain sight, much like a ball hidden in a person's pocket. The discussion transitions to the allegorical nature of descriptions of Heaven and Hell, with Dr. Khalifa positing that Hell is an exile from God in an eighth universe, characterized by darkness and distance rather than literal fire. The session concludes with reflections on the Quran's prophecies regarding the rejection of monotheism and the inevitability of the mathematical miracle becoming known worldwide, despite opposition from traditional religious authorities.

title: Quran Study 36 — Surah 30:25 — Miracle From Biggest Brewery, Intercession, Allegory (Feroz)
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa leads a study circle discussion focused on the mathematical proofs of the Quran and the nature of human ego as the primary obstacle to belief. He presents two new mathematical miracles involving the Quranic verse numbering system, arguing that when zeros are inserted to account for the Bismillah in each sura, the resulting sequence is a multiple of 19. He asserts that these structural miracles are distinct from the Quran's literary composition and are designed by God to leave no excuse for disbelievers. The discussion transitions to an analysis of Sura 7, verses 58 through 79, covering the missions of Noah, Hûd, and Sāleh. Dr. Khalifa argues that the rejection of these messengers by their people stems from the same human ego and idol worship present in the modern era. He contends that the intention behind one's actions only counts when those actions are already in accordance with God's commandments, dismissing the excuse that "intention is what matters" when a person associates other names with God. He further explores the concept of the ego as the ultimate idol, suggesting that humans are "miniature satans" who must overcome their pride to be redeemed. The session concludes with a brief exchange regarding the pre-existence of human souls and the covenant of God's absolute authority.

title: Quran Study 37 — Surah 11:68 (Shakira)
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa leads a study circle at Shakira Karipineni’s home, focusing on the Quranic verses 10:66 through 10:78. He opens by analyzing 10:68, arguing that God condemns the attribution of a son to Him, clarifying that while the righteous are metaphorically children of God, the literal claim is blasphemous. He discusses the history of Noah in 10:71-73, framing it as a recurring pattern where messengers face persecution from those who reject God's authority. The discussion shifts to the nature of retribution, with Dr. Khalifa explaining that believers will be spared the suffering destined for disbelievers, though he clarifies this does not mean the total eradication of the population. He addresses the concept of original sin in 10:74, asserting that humans are rebels who rejected God in a past life. The group engages in a lengthy dialogue regarding the mathematical miracle of the Quran, specifically the number 19, and its role in validating the number of units in the Contact Prayers. Dr. Khalifa critiques the omission of the opening verse, Bism Allah Arrahman Arraheem, in traditional prayers, labeling it a satanic innovation. The session concludes with a discussion on dietary laws, the prohibition of alcohol and gambling, and the importance of maintaining family harmony while sharing the message.

title: Quran Study 38 — Certainty (Parivash)
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa leads a study circle in Tucson, Arizona, focusing on the historical corruption of the Quran and the divine preservation of its text. He asserts that two false verses were added to the Quran during the reign of Uthman, triggering centuries of conflict and the eventual massacre of the Prophet's family. He argues that true believers are those who uphold the Quran alone, noting that mosques are now emerging where only the name of God is commemorated. Dr. Khalifa explains the mechanism for attaining certainty, citing Sura 15:99, and emphasizes the importance of performing the five daily prayers, fasting, and paying Zakat on the day of harvest. The group discusses the political system of consultation, the statistical reality of the Quran's preservation, and the nature of the jinn. Dr. Khalifa addresses questions about the definition of usury, the practice of Aqiqah as a superstition, and the historical evidence surrounding the removal of the two false verses from the Quran.

title: Quran Study 39 — Surah 60-61 — Rich Believer, Certainty, Insurance (Edip)
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa leads an extended study session focusing on Sura 60 and 61 of the Quran, emphasizing the necessity for believers to maintain a firm, public stand for God alone. He discusses the rules of engagement regarding non-believers, arguing that believers should remain equitable and kind toward those who do not actively fight them or evict them from their homes, while completely disassociating from those who demonstrate open hostility. The discussion shifts to the practical implications of these verses, with participants raising questions about personal relationships, the treatment of relatives who practice idolatry, and the handling of asylum seekers in times of conflict. Dr. Khalifa clarifies that the Quranic injunctions regarding war and the treatment of enemies are specific to religious persecution. The session also covers the glorification of God by all things in the universe, the condemnation of sectarianism, and the importance of consistency between one's words and actions. Later, the group engages in a lively debate regarding the status of rich versus poor believers, with Dr. Khalifa maintaining that the Quran explicitly identifies the rich believer as having greater potential for charity and support of the divine cause, provided they remain humble and focused on their duties. The session concludes with anecdotes about children and new believers demonstrating innate spiritual awareness, alongside a brief critique of traditional misinterpretations of Quranic verses.

title: Quran Study 40 — Surah 3:59 (Catherine)
description: In this study session, Dr. Rashad Khalifa and Catherine examine the theological implications of Sura 3:59-80, focusing on the nature of Jesus, the necessity of absolute submission to God, and the dangers of ego-driven religious distortion. Catherine leads the discussion by reflecting on the challenges of teaching the Quran to those outside the community, noting that the Quran serves as a living voice that requires constant, critical self-examination. She argues that the common human tendency to attribute events to other people—such as blaming a boss or a driver—is a failure to recognize God's absolute control. Dr. Khalifa reinforces this by emphasizing that the invitation in verse 64 to worship God alone is a logical, universal agreement that transcends sectarian divisions. The group discusses the historical fabrication of the Trinity, with Matt noting the political origins of the Nicene Creed, and Dr. Khalifa highlights that the term 'Ummiyyeen' in verse 75 refers to Gentiles, providing evidence that Prophet Muhammad was literate and wrote the Quran with his own hands. The session concludes with a critique of modern televangelists who manipulate scripture for financial gain, contrasting their behavior with the true, humble submission required of believers.

title: Quran Study 41 — Al-Fatiha For Everything You Wish, Extreme Libertarianism (Rashad)
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa leads a study session focused on Sura 54 of the Quran, "The Moon," interpreting the opening verse as a prophecy fulfilled by the lunar missions of the 1970s. He asserts that the mathematical code of the Quran provides physical evidence of God's existence, a claim he contrasts with the skepticism of those who dismiss such signs as magic. Khalifa discusses the nature of the soul, arguing that humans must nourish their eternal selves rather than merely their physical bodies, and he challenges traditional narratives surrounding Noah's Ark, describing the flood as a local event rather than a universal catastrophe. The session includes a detailed examination of the destruction of the peoples of ‘Ad and Thamûd, with Khalifa emphasizing that retribution is a consequence of human stubbornness and the rejection of divine warnings. The dialogue transitions into a technical debate regarding amino acids and messenger RNA, with Dr. Mahmoud Sabahi questioning the scientific accuracy of Khalifa's claims about the number 19 in biological systems. The session concludes with a discussion on the nature of freedom, government, and the Quranic perspective on individual choice, followed by a collective recitation of Al-Fatiha for the healing of a community member.

title: Quran Study 42 — Interview W/Rashad by Ray Caton, Insurance, Interest (Ray Caton)
description: In this discussion, Dr. Rashad Khalifa addresses an audience in Canada, emphasizing the necessity of absolute devotion to God alone as the sole purpose of human existence, as stated in Sura 51:56. He argues that Satan, or Iblis, actively deceives humanity by encouraging the worship of religious scholars, prophets, and saints, thereby leading people into hidden idol worship. Khalifa details three primary criteria for identifying such shirk, or idol worship, within oneself: feeling aversion when God alone is mentioned, experiencing comfort when other names are associated with God, and rejecting the Quran as the sole source of religious guidance. He cites various suras, including 39:45, 17:45, and 6:112-116, to illustrate how God places veils over the hearts of those who deny the Hereafter. Throughout the session, he fields questions from Ray Caton regarding the role of Ibrahim in establishing Islamic practices, the legitimacy of living in non-Islamic countries, the prohibition of usury and insurance, and the status of women in the mosque. Khalifa maintains that the Quran is fully detailed and complete, asserting that any religious practice not explicitly found within it, such as traditional nine-step ablution rituals, constitutes a deviation from God's law. He concludes by explaining the nature of free will and the purpose of human creation in the context of Satan's challenge to God's authority.

title: Quran Study 43 — Surah 17:39 — 3rd Intl Conf, Rashad Speech, Insurance Based On Fear (Edip)
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa delivers a lecture to his study circle in Tucson, Arizona, focusing on the necessity of worshiping God alone and following the Quran exclusively. He argues that the traditional Islamic Shahada, which includes the name of Muhammad, constitutes idolatry, a practice he claims God identified as a violation of His absolute kingship. Khalifa discusses the historical corruption of religious texts and practices, including the misinterpretation of Zakat and the incorrect performance of ablution. He presents mathematical evidence from the Quran, specifically regarding the word 'alone' (Wahdahu), to support his doctrine of Quranic supremacy. Throughout the session, he addresses the role of Satan in misleading humanity, the concept of the invisible barrier that prevents disbelievers from understanding the Quran, and the importance of being open-minded to God's messengers. The recording includes informal introductions of attendees, a demonstration of a bird singing in harmony with a Quranic recitation, and a Q&A session covering topics such as the jinn, phobias, and the interpretation of prostration in the story of Joseph.

title: Quran Study 44 — Surah 64 & 70 — Nothing Happens, Worry, Chastity (Rashad)
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa leads a study circle in Tucson, Arizona, focusing on the interpretation of Sura 64, "Mutual Blaming," and the nature of God's absolute authority. He emphasizes that all creation, including the human body, glorifies God, and he argues that God guarantees happiness and health to those who follow His commandments. He contrasts this with the Hadith, which he claims falsely suggests that the most righteous are the most miserable. Dr. Khalifa explains that the "Mutual Blaming" of the Day of Judgment refers to the accountability of individuals for their own actions, asserting that no one will be put in Hell against their will. He discusses the mathematical miracle of the Quran, specifically the frequency of the word "God," as proof of its divine origin. The session includes a segment where attendees discuss the distribution of spoils of war, the nature of hypocrisy, and the importance of unity among believers, illustrated by personal anecdotes of community support. Edip Yuksel joins the study to begin an analysis of Sura 70, exploring the relativity of time and the inevitable nature of the Day of Judgment, while Dr. Khalifa provides scientific analogies to explain the speed of light and the divine perspective on time.

title: Quran Study 45 — Surah 40 — Deja Vu, Old Believers Usually Finish All Affairs Before Departing (Rashad)
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa leads a study circle in Tucson, Arizona, focusing on the interpretation of Sura 40 and the mathematical miracle of the Quran. He emphasizes the significance of the initials "Ha Meem" in verses 40:1-40:6, arguing that their frequency in seven consecutive suras serves as divine proof of the Quran's authenticity. He discusses the historical persecution of prophets, specifically Muhammad, and asserts that those who reject the Quranic miracle or the messenger of the covenant are destined for Hell. The discussion shifts to the necessity of worshipping God alone, with Dr. Khalifa explaining that idol worship, including the mention of Muhammad or other figures in prayer, nullifies good works. He provides recent mathematical findings regarding the number of daily prayer units and Fatiha recitations, framing these as objective evidence. The group also explores the state of the soul after death, the nature of dreams, and the prohibition of dietary restrictions not explicitly ordained by God, which Dr. Khalifa characterizes as a form of idol worship.

title: Quran Study 46 — Surah 37:159 & 38:25 & 9:50 & 39:11 — Admission Test, No Insurance Compromise, Jinns, Hypocrites, Apology (Parivash)
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa leads a study circle in Tucson, Arizona, covering Sura 37:159 through 38:25, while addressing the nature of the jinn, the mechanics of divine protection, and the reality of the admission test for believers. He explains that jinns are creatures that attempt to mislead humans by impersonating historical figures or celebrities, yet he emphasizes that a believer can convert their assigned jinn companion by persistently reading and applying the Quran. Dr. Khalifa discusses the specific roles of angels in protecting those who invoke God's name, and he interprets the "dwellers of the Woods" mentioned in Sura 38 as the people of Midyan. Throughout the session, he addresses questions about the nature of happiness, the inevitability of retribution for those who reject the message, and the proper conduct for distributing charity, stressing that believers must prioritize relatives while maintaining absolute devotion to God alone. He also reflects on the story of David and the two brothers, using it to illustrate the necessity of careful, God-conscious judgment. The session concludes with a discussion on the hypocrites who infiltrate the community, the importance of not compromising God's law, and the ongoing struggle to align one's inner thoughts with divine guidance.

title: Quran Study 47 — Surah 1 & 2 — Intro to Blue Quran (Catherine)
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa introduces the "Blue Quran" project, a significant editorial and theological undertaking aimed at consolidating all of God's messages into a single, unified religion of total submission to God alone. He highlights the contributions of his study circle, specifically praising Lisa Spray for her editorial work and Edip Yuksel for his enlightenment regarding the status of Jews and Christians. Throughout the session, he emphasizes that the Quran is the final testament and that Islam is not a name but a description of submission. He discusses the mathematical miracle of the Quran, the role of the messenger of the covenant, and the necessity of rejecting all forms of idolatry, including the veneration of historical figures. The discussion includes a detailed reading of the introduction to the new translation, covering the history of the Heavenly dispute, the creation of humans and jinns as a test, and the significance of the age of forty. Dr. Khalifa also addresses the hostility he faces from traditionalists and clarifies that his followers do not follow him, but rather the word of God. The session concludes with a recitation of Sura Al-Fatiha and a preliminary study of the opening verses of Sura Al-Baqarah, focusing on the characteristics of believers, disbelievers, and hypocrites.

title: Quran Study 48 — Rashad's Speech — Salat, Zakat, Fazeli Argues (Edip)
description: In this 1989 session held in Tucson, Dr. Rashad Khalifa discusses the necessity of upholding God's absolute authority, framing the human experience as a second chance following a primordial "Great Feud" where creatures were swept into a crowd by Satan's false claims. He argues that the Five Contact Prayers and Zakat are essential gifts from God for soul development, rather than mere chores. Khalifa emphasizes that the Quran is fully detailed and that the Contact Prayers were established through Abraham, not invented by later traditions. The session includes a heated debate with a guest who defends the traditional practice of invoking Muhammad's name alongside God during prayer. Khalifa asserts that Muhammad is dead and unaware of such invocations, characterizing the addition of any name to God's as the unforgivable sin of shirk. He challenges the guest's reliance on Hadith, insisting that the Quran provides all necessary religious guidance.

title: Quran Study 49 — Rashad's Speech, 19 Math (Behrouz)
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa presents a lecture at a private home in Tucson, Arizona, on November 5, 1989, focusing on the mathematical structure of the Quran and the origin of human existence. He argues that the number 19 serves as a divine signature, citing the work of Rabbi Judah the Pious, who identified the number 19 as a key to the scriptures. Khalifa presents physical evidence of this mathematical code, including the number of verses, the frequency of the word "Allah," and the total of all numbers mentioned in the Quran. He posits that these findings are not human-made and have been rigorously scrutinized. Transitioning to theological questions, he explains that humans were originally angels in God's kingdom who rebelled alongside Satan due to ego. He describes the current world as an experimental environment where humans are given a second chance to denounce their rebellion and submit to God's absolute authority. Khalifa addresses audience questions regarding the existence of Satan, the nature of free will, and the innate instinct to search for the Creator, comparing the human condition to a test of loyalty.

title: Quran Study 50 — Surah 92-94 — Zakat Not Limited To Earned Income (Catherine)
description: Kathryn leads a study circle session on Suras 92, 93, and 94. She opens with Sura 92 (Al-Lail), interpreting night as an analogy for earthly existence blocking humanity from God's presence, and daylight as the revelation of truth on the Day of Resurrection. She reflects on human flaws described in the Quran and recounts personal experiences, including family Christmas gifts burdened by expectations, visiting the DeGrazia Gallery where a friend questioned spending thousands on paintings instead of aiding the poor, and contemplating guardian angels and jinns while driving with her son Jason. Edip Yüksel notes how Quranic contrasts mirror the dualities of human life. Dr. Rashad Khalifa explains that Sura 92 outlines the secret to true happiness, emphasizing that giving 2.5 percent in charity must be a continuous practice alongside prayer and daily self-care. A Q&A follows regarding obligations on unearned income, loans, evaluating beggars, and prioritizing relatives or local food banks over administrative charities. Kathryn moves to Sura 93 (Ad-Duha), discussing divine protection and recalling a trip where the group prayed amid desert mosquitoes. Dr. Khalifa, Mahmoud, and Edip debate whether verse 93:7 applies strictly to Muhammad or generally to all believers, noting traditionalist objections to claiming Muhammad was ever astray. Concluding with Sura 94 (Al-Inshirah), Kathryn shares a work incident at a hospital involving a disabled patient to illustrate emotional self-control, while Dr. Khalifa lightheartedly defends translating 94:5–6 as "With pain there is gain."

title: Quran Study 51 — Surah 17:59 (Edip)
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa leads a study circle discussion focused on the spiritual consequences of abandoning God, the nature of Satan's influence, and the interpretation of specific Quranic verses. He explains that the soul shrinks when one fails to worship God alone, drawing an analogy between the resulting negative energy and the violence depicted in Western films. The discussion shifts to the limitations of Satan, with Khalifa arguing that Satan is incompetent and often oblivious to God's work, citing his own discovery of the Quranic mathematical miracle while working at a brewery as a prime example of God hiding truth in plain sight. Participants engage in a dialogue regarding the nature of disasters, which Khalifa categorizes into admission tests, blessings in disguise, educational experiences, and divine retribution. He further discusses the role of messengers, the significance of the Five Prayers as a gift from God, and the process by which souls are assigned to newborns. The session concludes with a detailed examination of Sura 17:59-67, focusing on the obsolescence of physical miracles compared to the mental miracle of the Quran and the reality of Satan's attempts to entice humanity.

title: Quran Study 52 — Surah 1-2 (Iman)
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa leads a study circle focusing on the significance of Al-Fatiha as the essential, numerically structured key for establishing contact with God. He characterizes the Arabic sounds of the opening sura as a universal, non-language tool that believers must utilize in its original form to ensure their spiritual development. Khalifa argues that the contact prayer is a mechanical process, asserting that while Satan actively attempts to distract individuals, the efficacy of the prayer remains intact regardless of one's ability to concentrate. He addresses concerns regarding prayer during travel or unusual circumstances, citing Sura 2:239 to validate praying while walking or riding. The discussion shifts to the nature of divine inspiration versus satanic influence, with Khalifa maintaining that all things occur within God's will. Dr. Mahmoud Sabahi contributes by referencing Sura 40:16 to discuss the nature of kingship and judgment on the Day of Resurrection. The session concludes with a review of the sequence of Quranic revelation, where Khalifa outlines the progression from the first command to read, the second to write, and the subsequent revelation of the number 19 and the key of Al-Fatiha.
